title: 「동남아시아·동아시아·태평양 지역  스캠 대응 연락그룹회의 원칙 성명」 발표

The contribution will support STDF activities that help countries meet international food safety and animal and plant health standards, as well as facilitate safe and inclusive trade.

title: ‘I had a better life in Iran’: Afghan women forced home struggle to rebuild
description: For five years, Zahra cared for an elderly woman in Iran and earned enough to get by. Now back in Herat, western Afghanistan, the 28-year-old trained midwife is unemployed. She lives with her parents and siblings, apart from her six-year-old son, who lives with her ex-husband.

title: COP31 ends without climate pact as UN chief warns there is ‘no ambiguity in the science’
description: COP31 ended on Sunday without a climate pact after negotiators failed to overcome divisions over fossil fuels, bringing two weeks of talks and two days of overtime to a close that UN Secretary-General António Guterres described as a “deeply disappointing” setback.

title: ‘We escaped with only our lives’: Fighting to give birth in war-torn Yemen
description: When fighting suddenly escalated around Taiz, in southwestern Yemen two months ago, midwife Anisa Fadhl had no time to pack a bag before she fled, leaving behind her home and her clinic. Both were later looted and destroyed.

title: Homes abandoned, harvests failing: Haiti’s farmers rebuild amid violence, hunger and El Niño
description: Years of insecurity, violence perpetrated by murderous armed gangs and economic instability, combined with displacement, poor agricultural performance and climate shocks, have left millions of Haitians struggling to meet their food needs.

title: Bridgetown AI summit to tackle safety as risks outpace capacity to respond
description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres is heading to Barbados to co-host a special summit on artificial intelligence (AI) safety on Monday, aimed at closing the gap between accelerating risks and many countries’ capacity to deal with the pace of development.

title: ‘You will not be alone’: General Assembly President tells Rohingya refugees after genocide ruling
description: A day after the UN’s highest court found that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya, the President of the General Assembly visited the refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, urging the world to turn the landmark judgement into action.

title: West Bank: Record settler attacks mar olive harvest as UN urges Israel to protect farmers
description: Israeli settlers have carried out more than 400 attacks causing casualties or property damage during this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank – more than in any previous season, UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs said on Friday.

title: Shattered playgrounds and freezing classrooms: Inside Ukraine’s deadliest year for children
description: Amid the ruins of a twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten as a day-long power cut continued, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) on Friday highlighted the dangers to youngsters enduring another brutal winter in Ukraine, as child casualty numbers rise to record levels.

title: WFP plans to assist 91 million in 2027 as hunger crisis deepens
description: The World Food Programme (WFP) will require $12.1 billion to assist 91 million people next year but warned that millions more will go hungry as funding shortfalls continue and another global food crisis looms.

title: COP31: Countries demand stronger climate deal amid deadlock in Antalya
description: A group of countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific has challenged the proposed COP31 agreement, demanding explicit action on fossil fuels and stronger climate finance. With the summit due to close on Friday, tensions are rising as activists warn the talks are headed for failure, and negotiators search for a deal that nearly 200 governments can accept.

title: Afghanistan restrictions prevent pregnant women from seeking medical help
description: Aid and development agencies in Afghanistan warned on Friday of an escalating “assault” on the rights and freedoms of women and girls that is preventing growing numbers from accessing vital medical care.

title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
description: From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions. But these signals are increasingly being blocked or faked – and civilians are paying the price.

title: Peacekeeping: With 500 paternity and child support claims unresolved, UN scales up accountability
description: The UN is adding new accountability measures to better support children fathered by peacekeepers, the Under-Secretary-General for Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance, Catherine Pollard, announced Thursday.

title: ‘Losing the battle’: AI hands predators new ways to target children
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is handing predators and criminal groups new ways to groom, extort and exploit children, while efforts to protect them are failing to keep pace, senior UN officials warned on Thursday.

title: COP31: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
description: A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday. While activists delivered the message with humour, it reflected a serious concern: explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels had disappeared from the latest draft climate agreement. On the eve of the summit's scheduled close, ministers and the Presidency were still trying to bridge sharp differences as civil society groups pressed for stronger action.

title: No government approval needed to form or join a group, UN rights committee says
description: People do not need their government’s permission to form or join an association, the UN Human Rights Committee said on Thursday, issuing new guidance as civic space shrinks around the world.

title: World’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
description: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, delivered its judgment on Thursday in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar on the application of the Genocide Convention, finding Myanmar responsible for the crime against the country’s ethnic Rohingya, the first such ruling against a State.

title: COP31 deadlock persists as countries launch new ‘climate reality check’
description: With the clock running down at COP31 in Antalya, countries on Wednesday launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept, even as ministers remained deadlocked over some of the summit’s toughest questions: who pays, how fast the world moves away from fossil fuels and whether a greener future can be called “just” if poorer countries cannot afford it.

title: Patients running out of options as antibiotics stop working against common infections
description: Common bacteria are becoming highly resistant to front-line and even “last-resort” antibiotics, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Wednesday, warning that the situation today is worse than it was in 2019.

title: Dozens more children killed in Yemen amid escalating hostilities
description: The UN child rights agency, UNICEF, on Wednesday called for warring parties in Yemen to protect children as renewed conflict between Houthi rebels and Government forces approaches the three-month mark.

title: Ukraine: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
description: This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.

title: COP31: The push to protect warming oceans reaches the negotiating table
description: From identifying marine life with a cup of seawater to drawing on Indigenous knowledge to prevent wildfires, scientists and communities showcased both cutting-edge and time-tested ways to protect nature at COP31 on Tuesday. Yet turning innovation into action remains a challenge, with funding gaps persisting and ministers struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance as negotiations enter their final days.

title: Haiti: ‘Atrocious abuses’ continue as UN warns anti-gang operations must priortise civilian protection
description: The UN human rights office, OHCHR has urged greater protection for civilians in Haiti amid ongoing “atrocious abuses” committed by gangs and intensified security operations.

title: ‘Hunger should not be a concern’: WFP steps in for families in Kenya who fled Ethiopia violence

title: Winter rains deepen Gaza crisis amid restricted access and aid cuts
description: Gaza is facing a deepening shelter, sanitation and food security crisis as winter rains flood makeshift shelters, destroy scarce food supplies and leave displaced families struggling to stay warm and fed.

title: ‘Peace begins in our hearts’: Children close Muscat forum with a message to the world
description: Children from across the world sent a message of peace from the Omani capital Muscat on Monday, calling for an end to hatred, respect for diversity and the protection of human rights.

title: ‘An unfulfilled plan helps no one’: Superbug plans have doubled, but few countries are delivering
description: More countries are drawing up plans to tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR), but major gaps in testing and treatment mean billions of people continue to be at risk, according to new data released by the World Health Organization (WHO) on Monday.

title: Lebanon leading the way in mental health support
description: Mental health support must be a core part of the humanitarian response, said the UN Deputy Secretary-General during a visit to Lebanon over the weekend, where efforts to address the psychological toll of years of conflict and instability offer valuable lessons for other crisis-affected countries.

title: AI gets climate science right – until users push back
description: The best AI models answer most climate science questions correctly, but they often abandon established facts as soon as a user disagrees, according to a new report co-authored by the UN.
